badge.$comment: A word wearing a tone (0053). The box is text-sized — a badge stands on no control axis, because it is not a control — and every tone is one bg/fg/border triple: the base carries no suffix and is what a badge with no tone wears, and the four suffixed triples are the library's four tones (`PctTone`, 0076). They arrived in two goes: `danger` was here first, alone, because it was the only tone the skin had a colour for, and `success` / `warning` / `info` followed the ramps the button's tone axis landed (0082). The border is drawn under every tone for the forced-colours reason the chips wrote down: the fill is the first thing every flattening takes.
badge.$comment-radius: `radius.md` and deliberately not the chips' pill: a chip LOOKS grabbable because it is, and a word of status must not borrow that costume — the corner is the one visual cue telling the scanning eye which small box answers the pointer.

gap.$description: Gap between the badge's text and its icon.

badge.$comment-tones: Four triples, one shape: `{pct.<tone>}` for the fill, `{pct.on-<tone>}` for the word, and `{pct.<tone>}` again for the edge. The border is the same colour as the fill on purpose — the edge exists for the modes that drop the fill, and in the author palette it simply thickens the box by nothing. `danger` reads differently from the other three only in its history: it is the skin's error colour painting its first background, the return `semantic.light.json` promised, and for one release it was the only suffix here.
